subtitle: From Household Hearths to the Mothers’ Uprising

panels.shot: epic wide of a vast open-air market in Imphal, rows of women seated with wares, mountains hazy in the distance, low sun casting long shadows
panels.action: Ima Keithel Guardian sits upright amid hundreds of women vendors, baskets of rice and fish before her, as lines of Manipuri women stretch into the distance like an army holding the market ground.

dialogue.text: In Manipur’s valley, where kings summoned men to war, the women of Ima Keithel quietly built a market so strong that one day it would stop the colonial state in its tracks.

i18n.hi: मणिपुर की घाटी में, जहाँ राजा मर्दों को जंग पर बुलाते थे, इमा कैथल की औरतों ने चुपचाप ऐसा मज़बूत बाज़ार खड़ा किया कि एक दिन उसने हुकूमत को ही रोक दिया।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view over 16th-century Manipur valley, small settlements along fields, a palace complex at the centre, hills ringing the plain
panels.action: Terraced fields glow green around a compact palace town; tiny lines of men march on a dusty track while clusters of women work in the paddies and courtyards below.

dialogue.text: The chronicle Cheitharol Kumbaba speaks of 16th-century Manipur, when kings tightened lallup, the corvée that pulled men for war and state work, leaving fields and homes in women’s hands.

i18n.hi: इतिहास ग्रंथ ‘चеитारोल कुम्बाबा’ में 16वीं सदी का मणिपुर दर्ज है, जब राजाओं ने ‘लालुप’ कड़ा कर दिया—वह बेगार जो मर्दों को जंग और राजकाज में खींच ले जाती, खेत–घर औरतों के हवाले छोड़कर।

panels.shot: medium shot at ground level of men leaving a village, women standing at doorways watching, mountains framing the scene
panels.action: A file of bareheaded Manipuri men walks away towards the palace road with spears and packs, while Ima Keithel Guardian stands in a doorway, one child at her hip, watching them fade into the valley haze.

dialogue.text: Lallup drew men for months at a time to the king’s service. Behind them, wives, sisters and mothers balanced fields, granaries and kin, and soon found they must also handle trade and credit.

i18n.hi: लालुप मर्दों को महीनों के लिए राजसेवा में खींच ले जाता। पीछे रह गईं बीवियाँ, बहनें, माएँ—जिन्होंने खेत, कोठार, रिश्तेदारी संभाली, और जल्दी ही सौदा–सूद और उधार भी अपने हाथ में ले लिया।

panels.shot: close-up on hands, low angle from a mat on the floor, as rice, fish and cloth are sorted into baskets
panels.action: On a woven mat, Ima Keithel Guardian’s hands deftly heap rice into one basket, dried fish into another, and fold bright handwoven cloth, while faint smoke from a hearth curls behind her.

dialogue.text: From household surplus they built small circuits of exchange, taking rice, fish, handwoven cloth and forest produce to shared spaces that would harden over time into the great women’s markets of Imphal.

i18n.hi: घर की बचत से उन्होंने छोटे–छोटे लेन–देन के चक्कर बनाए, चावल, मछली, हाथ–कते कपड़े और जंगल की चीज़ें साझा जगहों पर ले आईं—जो धीरे–धीरे इम्फाल के बड़े औरतों के बाज़ारों में ढल गए।

panels.shot: wide shot of an early open marketplace near Khwairamband, women seated in rows, the royal road visible nearby, a few men passing through but not vending
panels.action: Rows of women sit on low platforms by the Khwairamband crossroad, their baskets laid out in front; a couple of male soldiers walk past on the road, glancing at this growing, ordered bustle they do not control.

dialogue.text: By the seventeenth century, as lallup hardened and the palace drew male labour, these women’s markets around Khwairamband became institutions, their order and rules defined by the women who ran them.

i18n.hi: सत्रहवीं सदी तक, जब लालुप और सख़्त हुआ और महल ने मर्द मज़दूर अपने पास खींच लिए, तब ख्वैराम्बंद के इर्द–गिर्द ये औरतों के बाज़ार मजबूत संस्थाएँ बन गए—जिनके क़ायदे–कानून चलाती थीं वही औरतें।

panels.shot: medium shot inside the market, low, intimate angle, women in semi-circle, one speaking, others listening, tally sticks or palm-leaf slips beside them
panels.action: Ima Keithel Guardian sits among a semi-circle of elders, one woman leaning forward to speak as others nod gravely, simple tally-sticks and small bundles of coins resting on the mats beside them.

dialogue.text: They set prices, extended credit, punished cheats and settled quarrels. No royal officer wrote these rules; the mothers’ unions, leikai by leikai, enforced them with reputation and collective strength.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने ही दाम तय किए, उधार दिया, ठगों को सज़ा दी और झगड़े निपटाए। कोई शाही अफ़सर इन नियमों का लेखक नहीं था—माएँ ही, लेikai–लेikai की यूनियन बनाकर, इज़्ज़त और सामूहिक ताकत से उन्हें लागू करती रहीं।

panels.shot: epic panoramic shot of Ima Keithel in the 19th century, dense with vendors and buyers, hills in background, palace spire distant
panels.action: The market sprawls like a living organism, hundreds of women in tight rows, paths of buyers weaving between them, while the far-off palace roof peeks above trees at the edge of the valley.

dialogue.text: By the nineteenth century, travellers and officials would note how these women controlled Imphal’s daily grain, fish and cloth, turning Ima Keithel into the valley’s beating economic heart.

i18n.hi: उन्नीसवीं सदी तक मुसाफ़िरों और अफ़सरों ने दर्ज किया कि कैसे ये औरतें इम्फाल का रोज़ का चावल, मछली और कपड़ा नियंत्रित करती हैं—इमा कैथल को घाटी का धड़कता आर्थिक दिल बना देती हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in from wide to medium on the market as sepia tones subtly shift to cooler, colonial-era palette, a few British and Assamese clerks visible on the edges
panels.action: The same bustling market now shows a handful of foreign-clad men with notebooks hovering on its fringes, while Ima Keithel Guardian watches them from her place on the mat, eyes narrowed in cautious curiosity.

dialogue.text: Then, in 1891, after war and defeat, Manipur fell under British political control. The palace lost power, but the women’s markets remained, now under the gaze of a new set of officials and traders.

i18n.hi: फिर 1891 में, जंग और हार के बाद, मणिपुर ब्रिटिश सियासी क़ाबू में आ गया। महल की ताकत घटी, पर औरतों के बाज़ार कायम रहे—अब नए अफ़सरों और सौदागरों की निगाहों के नीचे।

panels.shot: interior shot of the Political Agent’s bungalow, high angle, a British officer at a desk with a map and file, Manipuri interpreter nearby; through window, faint outline of market
panels.action: A British Political Agent bends over a map of Manipur, papers labelled for labour and supplies spread across his desk, while his Manipuri clerk points towards the window where the market’s roofs are just visible.

dialogue.text: British records from Imphal show a state keen to extract labour and timber, to build roads and bungalows cheaply. But village men were already bound by lallup; another source of unpaid work was needed.

i18n.hi: इम्फाल से ब्रिटिश काग़ज़ दिखाते हैं कि राज सस्ता मज़दूर और लकड़ी निचोड़ना चाहता था, सड़कें और बंगले खड़ा करना चाहता था। पर गांवों के मर्द पहले ही लालुप में बँधे थे—बेगार का नया ज़रिया चाहिए था।

panels.shot: wide street-level shot in 1904, colonial policeman reading an order to a group of bewildered men, women listening nearby in the market lane
panels.action: On a dusty lane near Khwairamband, a uniformed colonial policeman reads from a paper to a cluster of Manipuri men, while Ima Keithel Guardian and other women pause mid-sale, faces tightening as the words sink in.

dialogue.text: In 1904, an order required Manipuri men to cut and carry timber for colonial bungalows. For families already strained by lallup and loss, it meant more time away, more unpaid labour, more risk.

i18n.hi: 1904 में हुक्म आया कि मणिपुरी मर्द कॉलोनियल बंगलों के लिए लकड़ी काटें, ढोएँ। जो घर पहले ही लालुप और हानि से टूट रहे थे, उनके लिए यह और ज़्यादा दूर रहना, और बेगार, और खतरा था।

panels.shot: close-up on Ima Keithel Guardian rising from her mat, low angle making her loom slightly, other women turning towards her
panels.action: Ima Keithel Guardian pushes herself up from her mat, jaw set, as neighbouring vendors lay aside their measures of rice and turn towards her, attentive to the decision in her eyes.

dialogue.speaker: Ima Keithel Guardian
dialogue.text: If they take our men like this, who will stand for our homes?

i18n.hi: अगर वे हमारे मर्दों को यूँ ही उठा ले जाएँगे, तो हमारे घरों के लिए खड़ा कौन रहेगा?

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of a mass of women pouring out of Ima Keithel onto the main road, slightly low angle, colonial offices ahead
panels.action: A tide of Manipuri women, led by Ima Keithel Guardian, surges out from the market, wrappers hitched, hands raised, filling the street as they advance towards the whitewashed colonial buildings at the road’s end.

dialogue.text: What followed is remembered as the first Nupi Lan, the Women’s War. Hundreds of market women left their mats and marched on the British Residency, shouting that the timber order must be withdrawn.

i18n.hi: आगे जो हुआ, उसे पहली नूपी लान—औरतों की जंग—के नाम से याद किया जाता है। सैकड़ों बाज़ारिनें अपने चटाई छोड़कर ब्रिटिश रेजिडेंसी की तरफ़ कूच कर गईं, नारे लगाते कि लकड़ी वाला हुक्म वापस लो।

panels.shot: medium shot at the Residency gate, colonial officer behind gate, women massed outside, tension in their posture
panels.action: At the Residency gate, a British officer stands just inside with folded arms as Ima Keithel Guardian faces him through the bars, the press of women behind her taut as a drawn bow.

dialogue.text: British reports describe how the women surrounded the Residency and pressed the Political Agent for hours. With men unwilling to confront the state, it was the market that became the front line.

i18n.hi: ब्रिटिश रिपोर्टें लिखती हैं कि औरतों ने रेजिडेंसी घेर ली और घंटों पॉलिटिकल एजेंट पर दबाव बनाए रखा। मर्द राज्य से भिड़ने से हिचक रहे थे, तो मोर्चा बना खुद बाज़ार।

panels.shot: medium shot, side profile of officer and Ima Keithel Guardian, officer’s expression shifting from irritation to calculation
panels.action: In profile, the officer glances past Ima Keithel Guardian at the sea of women beyond, their eyes unwavering, and his own expression shifts from irritation to wary calculation.

dialogue.text: The timber order was modified, and the crisis ebbed. The files speak of ‘mob women’ and ‘agitation’, but behind those words lay a simple fact: the mothers’ market had forced the state to step back.

i18n.hi: लकड़ी का हुक्म बदला गया और टकराव कुछ थमा। फ़ाइलें ‘उपद्रवी औरतों’ और ‘आंदोलन’ लिखती हैं, पर उनके पीछे सच यही था—माओं के बाज़ार ने राज्य को पीछे हटने पर मजबूर किया।

panels.shot: dissolve-style wide shot of the market back in activity, but with an undercurrent, women talking as they work, subtle sense of new confidence
panels.action: Ima Keithel Guardian returns to her mat, measuring rice for a customer; around her, women lean towards one another in low conversation even as their hands continue their practised trade.

dialogue.text: After 1904, the market resumed its daily rhythm. Yet something had changed: economic power had revealed itself as political power, and the women had learned how quickly they could summon one another.

i18n.hi: 1904 के बाद बाज़ार ने फिर रोज़मर्रा की चाल पकड़ ली। पर अब एक बात बदल चुकी थी—आर्थिक ताकत ने अपना राजनीतिक चेहरा दिखा दिया था, और औरतें सीख चुकी थीं कि वे एक–दूसरे को कितनी जल्दी जुटा सकती हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Imphal in late 1930s, godowns and rice mills near railway line or cart road, loaded carts leaving, sky overcast
panels.action: Large rice godowns stand near the road out of Imphal as carts, heaped with sacks of paddy, creak away from the valley; Ima Keithel Guardian watches from a distance, clouds hanging low and heavy above.

dialogue.text: In the late 1930s, global war and markets brought new pressures. Rice mills and godowns in Imphal began to purchase grain for export, even as rumours of scarcity spread through the hills and valley.

i18n.hi: 1930 के आख़िर में, जंग और वैश्विक बाज़ार ने नए दबाव ला दिए। इम्फाल के चावल के मिल और गोदाम बाहर भेजने के लिए अनाज खरीदने लगे, जबकि घाटी–पहाड़ में कमी की अफ़वाहें फैल रही थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot inside Ima Keithel, women anxious, a customer arguing over higher price, baskets less full than before
panels.action: In Ima Keithel, baskets of rice sit noticeably lower; a customer gestures angrily at a price, while Ima Keithel Guardian and her neighbours trade worried looks over their thinning stock.

dialogue.text: As rice moved out under trade licences, the price in the market rose. For women responsible for feeding households and neighbourhoods, the link between distant policies and their daily measures of grain was immediate.

i18n.hi: जैसे–जैसे चावल लाइसेंस लेकर बाहर निकला, बाज़ार में उसके दाम चढ़ गए। घरों और मोहल्लों को खिलाने की ज़िम्मेदार औरतों के लिए दूर बैठी नीतियाँ और उनकी रोज़ की माप–तौल के बीच का रिश्ता एकदम साफ़ हो गया।

panels.shot: close-up on a secretive evening meeting in the market hall, low light, women in tight circle, one whispering urgently
panels.action: Under the dim light of an oil lamp in the emptied market, Ima Keithel Guardian sits in a tight circle of elders, one woman leaning close to whisper as others listen, their shadows long on the wooden floor.

dialogue.text: They held night meetings under the emptied roofs, debating grain control and export. Kamei’s account and colonial files agree: it was again the women vendors who first organised to confront the administration.

i18n.hi: वे खाली पड़े छप्परों के नीचे रात में बैठकें करने लगीं, अनाज नियंत्रण और निर्यात पर बहस करने लगीं। कामेई की लिखावट और कॉलोनियल फ़ाइलें एक बात पर सहमत हैं—फिर वही बाज़ारिनें सबसे पहले इकट्ठी होकर हुकूमत का सामना करने निकलीं।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of women blocking a road near a rice mill, carts halted, mill building beyond, stormy sky
panels.action: A line of women, Ima Keithel Guardian among them, stands firm across the road outside a rice mill, palms outstretched to stop oncoming bullock carts piled with sacks, dark clouds massing overhead.

dialogue.text: In 1939, they acted. The second Nupi Lan saw thousands of women picket rice mills, block roads and surround offices, demanding that rice exports stop until the valley’s own needs were secured.

i18n.hi: 1939 में उन्होंने कदम उठा लिया। दूसरी नूपी लान में हज़ारों औरतों ने चावल मिलों के बाहर धरना दिया, रास्ते ब्लॉक किए, दफ़्तरों को घेर लिया—मांग यही कि घाटी का पेट भरने तक चावल बाहर न जाए।

panels.shot: medium shot of protest outside the Durbar or secretariat, British officer trying to speak, women shouting slogans
panels.action: Outside the Durbar hall, a British officer raises his hands to address the crowd, but his words are drowned as Ima Keithel Guardian and the assembled women call out in unison, faces intent and unyielding.

dialogue.text: British reports from Imphal describe days of sustained protest around the Durbar, mills and offices. The women rejected partial promises, insisting that policy change, not persuasion, was needed to protect food.

i18n.hi: इम्फाल की ब्रिटिश रिपोर्टें लिखती हैं कि कैसे दरबार, मिलों और दफ़्तरों के चारों तरफ़ कई दिन तक घेरा और प्रदर्शन चलता रहा। औरतों ने अधूरे वादे ठुकरा दिए—कहा कि सिर्फ़ मनुहार नहीं, नीति बदलेगी तो ही अनाज बचेगा।

panels.shot: tense medium-wide shot as colonial police advance with lathis, women still sitting or standing, some shielding their heads
panels.action: Colonial policemen advance with raised lathis towards a seated line of women protesters; Ima Keithel Guardian stays upright, one arm lifted to shield her head, while others huddle together yet do not scatter.

dialogue.text: The files speak of lathi charges and arrests; contemporary accounts recall injuries and at least some deaths as the confrontation turned harsh. Yet the women’s resolve and numbers forced the crisis into official debate.

i18n.hi: फ़ाइलों में लाठीचार्ज और गिरफ़्तारियों का ज़िक्र है; उस दौर की यादों में जख्मों और कुछ मौतों तक का ब्योरा है, जब टकराव कड़ा हुआ। पर औरतों की जिद और तादाद ने इस संकट को मजबूरन सरकारी बहस का मुद्दा बना दिया।

panels.shot: somber medium shot in a courtyard, women tending to an injured protester, others looking towards the city where mills stand
panels.action: In a quiet courtyard, Ima Keithel Guardian supports an older woman with a bandaged head, while others look towards the distant outline of mills and offices, their faces marked by exhaustion and dogged purpose.

dialogue.text: The immediate gains were mixed: exports were restricted and policies adjusted, but colonial authority remained. Yet from this Nupi Lan emerged new leaders and networks that later joined wider anti-colonial politics.

i18n.hi: तुरंत के नतीजे मिले–जुले थे—निर्यात पर कुछ रोक लगी, नीतियाँ बदलीं, पर कॉलोनियल हुकूमत कायम रही। मगर इसी नूपी लान से नए नेता और नेटवर्क निकले, जो आगे चलकर बड़े आज़ादी आंदोलन से जुड़ गए।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot transitioning from 1940s to present-day Ima Keithel, structures updated but same dense female presence
panels.action: The market dissolves through time: wooden sheds give way to masonry halls and present-day structures, yet the scene remains constant—rows upon rows of women, including a modern echo of Ima Keithel Guardian, tending their stalls.

dialogue.text: Decades later, decolonisation came and Manipur’s politics shifted. But Ima Keithel endured, not as a relic but as a living institution where economic cooperation and protest memory still shape how women face new crises.

i18n.hi: दशकों बाद आज़ादी आई और मणिपुर की सियासत बदली। पर इमा कैथल बचा रहा—सिर्फ़ एक निशानी नहीं, बल्कि ज़िंदा संस्था की तरह, जहाँ आर्थिक साझेदारी और विरोध की यादें आज भी औरतों को नई मुश्किलों में रास्ता दिखाती हैं।

panels.shot: closing low-angle medium shot of Ima Keithel Guardian seated calmly amid the market, subtle superimposed impression of marching women behind her
panels.action: Ima Keithel Guardian sits composed on her mat in the bustling market, while behind her, like a faint overlay, the marching lines of 1904 and 1939 women seem to walk again through the valley air.

dialogue.text: From lallup’s burdens to Nupi Lan’s uprisings, the women of Ima Keithel turned the work of feeding families into a power that could challenge kings and colonisers—a reminder that markets, too, can become arenas of courage.

i18n.hi: लालुप के बोझ से लेकर नूपी लान की बगावतों तक, इमा कैथल की औरतों ने घर–घर का पेट भरने की मेहनत को ऐसी ताकत में बदला, जो राजा और हुक्मरानों को चुनौती दे सके—ये याद दिलाने को कि बाज़ार भी बहादुरी के अखाड़े बन सकते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Household Hearths to the Mothers’ Uprising
subtitle_i18n.hi: चूल्हे से उठी माओं की बगावत
